A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of single-qubit X gates, two-qubit CZ gates, tunable coupling and classical LQR control, including adaptation curves and baseline comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds empirical PL-condition diagnostics, adaptation-budget prediction results and conditioning-versus-adaptation experiments in Appendices A.7–A.9.

M1.justification: Section 5.4 and Algorithm 1 add an operational decision procedure: take 3–5 probe steps, fit the saturation model, flag poor fits, assess expected benefit and select an adaptation budget. This substantively extends deployment beyond v1's budget formula, while retaining the FOMAML architecture, training and gradient updates.

E1.justification: The X-gate, CZ-gate, tunable-coupler and LQR tasks remain. Coverage expands within quantum calibration to missing or 30%-noisy task descriptors and explicit 2×–5× OOD conditions for budget prediction; no new application domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table A.5 adds blind controllers with and without adaptation and noisy-context adaptation as controls against full FOMAML. The original fixed-average and GRAPE comparisons remain unchanged; conditioning-only corresponds to the existing no-adaptation strategy.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate budget-prediction relative error using 3, 4 or 5 probes, sweep PL thresholds using normalized per-task loss windows, and compare context access with K=30 adaptation while holding architecture and optimizer fixed. Existing training and simulation settings in Tables A.1–A.2 and Appendix D are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices A.7–A.9 add substantial analyses of PL satisfaction under distribution shift, sensitivity of budget prediction to probe count and OOD severity, and the separate contributions of conditioning and adaptation, including noisy descriptors. The earlier training diagnostics, variance analysis and learning-rate ablation remain.

E5.justification: No seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or revised error-band definitions are introduced. The new budget-prediction errors measure predictive accuracy, while task distributions and graphical spread continue the existing descriptive reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original results remain, including CZ fidelity of 54.2% before adaptation and 95.7% after K=10. New Table A.4 reports budget errors of 2.9–19.2% with five probes versus 36.7–47.5% with three. Table A.5 adds adaptation-only gains of 0.184 and 0.158 over blind baselines, alongside new PL-distribution results.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 expands the PL-only convergence argument to a KL condition with exponent alpha, adding descent recurrences and a polynomial residual bound for alpha greater than 1/2, with PL recovered at 1/2. The original PL theorem and task-variance derivation remain; Section 4.4 also clarifies their distinct assumptions.

C1.justification: v4 adds few-shot adaptation-budget prediction as a central contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. It also claims a KL extension and that adaptation without task descriptors explains much of recovery under shift. The original exponential-saturation, variance-scaling and quantum/LQR validation claims are retained.

C2.justification: v4 introduces interpretations of graceful PL degradation, adaptation versus conditioning, and tolerance to imperfect task descriptors. It develops simulate-then-deploy applicability, PL-fit diagnostics and a KL fallback, and broadens the hardware discussion to simulator mismatch and finite-shot noise. The stationary-noise restriction remains in the introduction.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and specifies probe-fitting rules, normalized PL estimation, zeroed task features and multiplicative Gaussian descriptor noise. Existing architecture, optimizer, integration and simulation-parameter tables are retained. The linked repository's contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: New references support KL convergence and hardware applicability, including Attouch, Alexeev, Yang, Carroll, Klimov and Krantz. These strengthen the simulate-then-deploy positioning and motivation for noise shifts, while the main comparisons with MAML theory, GRAPE and metaQctrl remain.

P1.justification: The contributions, theoretical explanations, limitations and conclusion receive targeted rewrites, and some appendix commentary is shortened. Section 5.4 and Appendices A.7–A.9 are added, but the main section sequence and overall Appendix A–D organization remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds a substantial workflow diagram, multipanel Figures A.7–A.9, two new result tables and main-text decision-protocol pseudocode. The theoretical-verification table gains a PL-breadth row. Existing main figures are retained as Figures 2–6, with relocation and caption edits rather than replacement.

improvement.justification: The decision protocol, conditioning ablation and broader PL diagnostics make v1's practical guidance more actionable and better supported. However, the abstract overgeneralizes prediction accuracy: Table A.4 supports 3–19% error only with five probes, while three give 36.7–47.5%. Figure A.7 also contains R² values below 0.95 despite stronger textual summaries. These new inconsistencies temper the useful additions, supporting a limited net improvement.
